# ReadmeGenAI

> ReadmeGenAI is a free, open-source web app that generates professional README.md files from GitHub repository metadata and file structure.

## Overview

ReadmeGenAI helps developers create a structured README for a GitHub repository. Enter a repository URL, choose an output language, and the app uses Google Gemini to generate Markdown that can be reviewed and used in the project.

The app supports public repositories. Private repositories require GitHub sign-in and explicit consent before repository metadata and file names are sent to the AI model.

## How generation works

1. The user submits a GitHub repository URL and selects an output language.
2. The app validates the URL and retrieves repository metadata and a list of repository file paths through GitHub's API.
3. The app uses that metadata and file list as context for Google Gemini.
4. Gemini returns README content as Markdown for the user to review.

The current generation route builds its prompt from repository description, primary language, license, root file paths, and simple technology indicators. It does not send source file contents to the model.

## Supported output languages

English, Danish, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, and Turkish.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://readmegen-ai.vercel.app/): Product overview and introduction to AI-generated GitHub READMEs.
- [Generate](https://readmegen-ai.vercel.app/generate): Submit a GitHub repository URL and generate a README.
- [Features](https://readmegen-ai.vercel.app/features): Overview of generation, GitHub integration, and repository-context features.
- [Examples](https://readmegen-ai.vercel.app/examples): Example README outputs.
- [Documentation](https://readmegen-ai.vercel.app/docs): Quick start, usage guidance, and frequently asked questions.

## Technology

- Next.js App Router and React
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Octokit for GitHub API access
- Google Gemini API for README generation
- NextAuth for GitHub sign-in
- Vercel Analytics

## Local development

The project uses npm. Install dependencies with `npm install`, then start the local development server with `npm run dev`. The app runs at `http://localhost:3000` by default. Some integrations require environment configuration; consult the repository documentation and deployment settings.
